cases.exposure_context_quote: A 78-year-old man with no known comorbidities or medication history was transferred to the emergency department of a tertiary care institute in Uttarakhand after ingestion of 50-mL chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin at his home.
cases.agent_quote: after ingestion of 50-mL chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin at his home
cases.circumstance: ingestion at home; intent not stated in text

symptoms.quote: After ingestion, he had multiple episodes of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting and was immediately taken to the local hospital.
the patient was transferred to the emergency department and arrived in an unconscious state
His vital signs were blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 104 beats/minute, and respiratory rate 24 breaths/minute.
Central nervous system examination showed bilateral 1-mm pinpoint pupils not reactive to light.

symptoms.finding: bilateral basal crackles and decreased breath sounds on the right
symptoms.quote: Respiratory system examination showed bilateral basal crackles and decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest.

Chest radiography displayed right-sided pneumothorax for which intercostal tube was inserted as shown in Figure 1. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax revealed right-sided pneumothorax with 5-mm pneumomediastinum.

cases.time_to_care: immediately taken to the local hospital after vomiting; then transferred to emergency department

labs.name: hematology and liver tests
labs.value: normocytic normochromic anemia with neutrophilic leukocytosis and mild transaminitis (detailed values in Table 1 not present in text)
labs.quote: Laboratory investigations revealed normocytic normochromic anemia with neutrophilic leukocytosis and mild transaminitis as shown in Table 1 (Case 1).

treatment.name: gastric lavage (local hospital)
treatment.quote: Gastric lavage was performed there, and then the patient was transferred to the emergency department and arrived in an unconscious state.

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation (VCAC, FiO2 100%, Vt 360 mL, PEEP 5 cm H2O)
treatment.quote: Etomidate and rocuronium were administered, and the patient was intubated with these settings: volume control assist control (VCAC) mode, fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) 100%, tidal volume (Vt) 360 mL, respiratory rate 16 breaths/minute, and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H2O

treatment.name: atropine 30 mg plus atropine infusion 6 mg/h
treatment.quote: the patient was atropinized with 30 mg atropine and atropine infusion was initiated at 6 mg/h

treatment.name: ceftriaxone 1 g twice daily and clindamycin 600 mg twice daily
treatment.quote: Ceftriaxone 1 g twice daily and clindamycin 600 mg twice daily were also started.

treatment.name: intercostal/thoracostomy tube for pneumothorax
treatment.quote: A thoracostomy tube was placed for the right-sided pneumothorax.

cases.outcome_quote: On day three, the patient died.
cases.notes: Pneumothorax/pneumomediastinum developed on day three with sudden rise in plateau (36 cm H2O) and peak (42 cm H2O) pressures; lung ultrasound showed lung point sign.

cases.exposure_context_quote: A 20-year-old woman with no known comorbidities or medication history was transferred to the emergency department of a tertiary care institute in Uttarakhand after ingestion of 30 mL chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin at her home.
cases.agent_quote: after ingestion of 30 mL chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin at her home
cases.circumstance: ingestion at home; intent not stated in text

symptoms.quote: After ingestion, she had multiple episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting, and became drowsy.
After ingestion, she had multiple episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting, and became drowsy.
She also experienced shortness of breath, increased lacrimation, salivation, and involuntary passage of stools.
She also experienced shortness of breath, increased lacrimation, salivation, and involuntary passage of stools.
She also experienced shortness of breath, increased lacrimation, salivation, and involuntary passage of stools.
with oxygen saturation 68% on room air and 98% with 4-L oxygen nasal prongs
Respiratory system examination showed bilateral basal crackles.
On day three, HRCT of the thorax revealed bilateral pneumothorax with left parasternal 39.7 mm pneumomediastinum as shown in Figure 2.

cases.time_to_care: immediately taken to the local hospital where gastric lavage was performed, then transferred to the emergency department

labs.name: hematology, liver tests, INR
labs.value: anemia with neutrophilic leukocytosis, mild transaminitis, and an increased international normalized ratio (detailed values in Table 1 not present in text)
labs.quote: Laboratory investigations revealed anemia with neutrophilic leukocytosis, mild transaminitis, and an increased international normalized ratio as shown in Table 1 (Case 2).

treatment.name: gastric lavage (local hospital)
treatment.quote: She was immediately taken to the local hospital where gastric lavage was performed, and then the patient was transferred to the emergency department.

treatment.name: atropine 12 mg plus atropine infusion 2.4 mg/h
treatment.quote: the patient was atropinized with 12-mg atropine and started on atropine infusion at 2.4 mg/h

treatment.name: noninvasive ventilation then intubation and mechanical ventilation
treatment.quote: She was initially placed on noninvasive ventilation due to increased work of breathing (FiO2 100%, PEEP 6 cm H2O, pressure support 8 cm H2O).

treatment.name: pralidoxime 2 g twice daily
treatment.quote: Pralidoxime 2 g twice daily, ceftriaxone 1 g twice daily, and clindamycin 600 mg twice daily were started.

treatment.name: ceftriaxone 1 g twice daily and clindamycin 600 mg twice daily
treatment.quote: Pralidoxime 2 g twice daily, ceftriaxone 1 g twice daily, and clindamycin 600 mg twice daily were started.

treatment.name: conservative management of pneumothorax; pigtail insertion for pneumomediastinum drainage
treatment.quote: The bilateral pneumothorax was managed conservatively. Pigtail insertion was performed for pneumomediastinum drainage.

cases.outcome: recovered; discharged on day 25, asymptomatic at follow-up
cases.outcome_quote: On day 25, she remained stable and maintained normal vital signs on room air, and was discharged. The patient is now asymptomatic with regular follow-up in the general medicine outpatient department.
cases.notes: Extubated day 12; repeat HRCT day 19 showed resolution; pigtail drain removed day 22.
